summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of tungsten nitride (W 1.5N) films as a diffusion barrier for Cu metallization. The process uses a pulse sequence of WF6/NH3/C2H4/SiH4/NH3 at 350°C. The films show low roughness, stable resistivity, and excellent diffusion barrier properties against Cu. The ALD process results in W 1.5N films with a composition of a mixture of WN and W2N phases, and the films are nonreactive with Cu up to 500°C.
evidence: An atomic layer deposition process to grow tungsten nitride films was established at 350°C with a pulse sequence of WF6/NH3/C2H4/SiH4/NH3. The film composition was determined with Rutherford backscattering as W 1.5N, being a mixture of WN and W2N phases. The resistivity of the films was stable after 50 cycles at a value of 480 mV cm. Results of four-point probe sheet resistance measurements at elevated temperature demonstrated that our films are nonreactive with Cu at least up to 500°C.
